titles.274: Annotatio V §.II cont open: True divine Fundamentals make the limits — proved Autoritative and Ratiocinative
titles.275: Annotatio V §.II Autoritative (Eph. 4): Keep the Spirit’s unity in the bond of peace — one body and one Spirit
titles.276: Annotatio V §.II Autoritative (Eph. 4): One Lord, faith, baptism, God — yet diverse gifts for building the body
titles.277: Annotatio V §.II Autoritative (Eph. 4): Unto the unity of the faith and the perfect man — truthing in love
titles.278: Annotatio V §.II Ratiocinative: Unanimous in fundamentals — one spiritual body more than not, though lesser dissent remains
titles.279: Annotatio V §.II Ratiocinative close: Church members who keep essentials — even amid many non-overturning errors — stop before §.IV

latin.274: Eadem verò Fundamentalia vera divinaque, Consociationis Ecclesiasticae limites conficere, probatur, tàm Autoritative, quam Ratiocinative.
latin.275: Autoritative ex Cap. 4. ad Ephes., rei probandae Loco quasi Communi reputando, totum insuper Fundamentum tàm Theoreticum à v. 1. ad 17. quàm Practicum à v. 17. ad fin. Cap. complexo, quando Apostolus v. 3. jubet servare unitatem Spiritûs in vinculo pacis, & unum Corpus Spiritumque, unum Corpus Spirituale constitui affirmat, ubi unus est Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus & Pater omnium, qui est super omnes & per omnes & in omnibus v. 4. 5. 6.;
latin.276: licèt deinceps & quod reliquum est, unicuique gratia data, etiam diversi gradûs, sit, secundum mensuram doni Christi v. 7. & alii constituti sint Apostoli, alii Prophetae v. 11. idque ad οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ad aedificationem Corporis Christi v. 12.
latin.277: quò καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ ὑιοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον, donec perveniamus omnes ad unam fidem [puta in omnibus & singulis] & in perfectum virum evadamus v. 13. non dimovendum vel circumagitandum omni ventô Doctrinae v. 14. intereà ἀληθεύοντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ in Charitate Veritati studentes v. 15.
latin.278: Ratiocinative: Quia in Fundamentalibus eoque necessariis praecipuisque Christianae Religionis dogmatibus unanimes, licèt in aliis minus fundamentalibus minusque necessariis dissentientes, ad majorem intereà perfectamque Unitatem contendentes, in Charitate, unum idemque Spirituale Corpus magis sunt, quàm non sunt; vel (quod eodem recurrit) unius ejusdemque Ecclesiae Christianae Consociatione continentur magis, quàm non continentur: Quandoquidem à potiori fit denominatio.
latin.279: Sicuti verò hominibus accensentur & societate humana eâdem contineri putantur, qui corpore & animâ rationali praediti sunt, licèt quandoque & animae rationalis vis virtusque exigua perquam, & Corporis membra nonnulla multum deformata inveniantur; ita ejusdem Consociationis Ecclesiasticae participes aestimandi, qui Ecclesiae Christianae essentialia, tàm Theoretica, quam Practica servant, licèt cum erroribus pariter atque peccatis Christianam Religionem haud evertentibus, etiam benè multis, colluctentur.

pass_a.274: But that the same true and divine Fundamentals make the limits of Ecclesiastical Consociation is proved both Autoritatively and Ratiocinatively.
pass_a.275: Autoritative from Ephesians chapter 4, to be reckoned as a quasi-common place of the thing to be proved, embracing besides the whole Foundation both Theoretical from v. 1 to 17 and Practical from v. 17 to the end of the chapter — when the Apostle in v. 3 bids keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace, and affirms one Body and Spirit, one Spiritual Body to be constituted, where there is one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in all (vv. 4–6);
pass_a.276: although next, and as for what remains, grace is given to each, even of diverse degree, according to the measure of the gift of Christ (v. 7), and some are set as Apostles, others as Prophets (v. 11), and that for the οἰκοδομή of the body of Christ — for the edification of the Body of Christ (v. 12).
pass_a.277: until we all arrive at the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man — until we all come to one faith [namely in all and each] and become a perfect man (v. 13), not to be moved or tossed about by every wind of Doctrine (v. 14), meanwhile ἀληθεύοντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ — studying Truth in Charity (v. 15).
pass_a.278: Ratiocinative: Because those unanimous in the Fundamental and so necessary and chief dogmas of the Christian Religion, though dissenting in others less fundamental and less necessary, yet striving meantime toward a greater and perfect Unity, in Charity, are more one and the same Spiritual Body than they are not; or (what comes to the same) are more contained in the Consociation of one and the same Christian Church than they are not — seeing that denomination is from the greater part.
pass_a.279: And just as those endowed with body and rational soul are counted among humans and thought to be contained in the same human society, even when sometimes both the force and virtue of the rational soul are very slight, and some members of the Body are found much deformed; so those are to be reckoned sharers of the same Ecclesiastical Consociation who keep the essentials of the Christian Church, both Theoretical and Practical, though they wrestle with errors and sins alike that do not overturn the Christian Religion — even with a good many of them.

274: That the same true, divine Fundamentals set the limits of church Consociation is proved two ways — by authority and by reason.
275: By authority: take Ephesians 4 as a standing commonplace for the point — covering the whole foundation, theoretical (vv. 1–17) and practical (v. 17 to the chapter’s end).

There the Apostle bids us keep the Spirit’s unity in the bond of peace (v. 3), and affirms one body and one Spirit — one spiritual body — where there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, above all, through all, and in all (vv. 4–6).
276: Yet afterward, and for what remains, grace is given to each — even in different measures — according to Christ’s gift (v. 7).
Some are set as apostles, others as prophets (v. 11), and that for the building up of Christ’s body (v. 12).
277: The aim is that we all arrive at the unity of the faith and the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a full-grown man (v. 13) — not tossed by every wind of teaching (v. 14) —
meanwhile speaking truth in love, studying truth in charity (v. 15).
278: By reason: those agreed on the fundamental — and so necessary and chief — dogmas of the Christian religion, though they still differ on lesser points, yet press on toward fuller unity in charity.
They are more one spiritual body than not.
Or, what comes to the same, they are more held in the Consociation of one Christian church than they are shut out of it — for we name a thing from its greater part.
279: Just as people with a body and a rational soul still count as human and as members of one society — even when the soul’s force is weak and some bodily members are badly misshapen —
so those who keep the church’s essentials, theoretical and practical, should be counted sharers in the same church Consociation,
even while they wrestle with many errors and sins that do not overturn the Christian religion.
Stop before §. IV (consensus and Consociation judged from the same fundamental principle).

notes.277: Eph 4:13–15; unity of faith; truthing in love.
notes.279: Human-society analogy; keep essentials amid non-overturning faults; stop before §.IV.
